Get started with easyNIS

Source: vignettes/getting-started.Rmd
getting-started.Rmd

This guide opens invented discharges, defines a diagnosis cohort, builds a survey design, estimates weighted summaries, and checks disclosure. All input comes from nis_example(); it contains no real NIS records and results are for learning only.

Open annual data

nis_open() scans Parquet files lazily. Collect only a small summary when you need to inspect records.

nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019:2020))
nis |> dplyr::count(YEAR) |> dplyr::collect()
#> # A tibble: 2 × 2
#>    YEAR     n
#>   <int> <int>
#> 1  2019    96
#> 2  2020    96

The counts here describe the synthetic fixture by year. See Opening NIS data for column selection, engines, and year coverage.

Define a cohort

Flags check each diagnosis slot independently. Prefixes are analyst supplied; easyNIS does not choose a clinical definition.

nis <- nis |> nis_flag_dx(heart_failure = "I50")
nis |> dplyr::count(heart_failure) |> dplyr::collect()
#> # A tibble: 2 × 2
#>   heart_failure     n
#>   <lgl>         <int>
#> 1 TRUE            108
#> 2 FALSE            84

The two rows show fixture records with and without a matching code. Review positions and code-system assumptions before using a flag; see Defining cohorts.

Build a survey design

The cohort is declared inside nis_design(). This preserves sampled hospital-year information when no discharges meet the cohort.

design <- nis_design(
  nis,
  cohort = heart_failure & AGE >= 18,
  keep = c(AGE, FEMALE, LOS),
  annualize = TRUE
)
#> Cohort: 108 discharges; weighted N 62.4; 18 hospitals across 2 years.

For a pooled design, annualize = TRUE divides discharge weights by the number of valid years. The rule treats each included year as a whole year; read Survey design and weighting before choosing it for a real analysis.

Estimate weighted summaries

Use survey-aware summaries so standard errors account for strata and hospitals.

srvyr::summarise(
  design,
  discharges = srvyr::survey_total(),
  mean_los = srvyr::survey_mean(LOS)
)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>   discharges discharges_se mean_los mean_los_se
#>        <dbl>         <dbl>    <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1       62.4          8.67     5.66       0.229

The estimated total and mean describe the fixture under its design fields, not national estimates. The standard errors are design based; ordinary row-level summaries would not represent this sampling design.

Review disclosure

nis_cell_counts() reports unweighted discharges and distinct year-scoped hospitals for each output cell.

records <- dplyr::collect(nis)
cells <- nis_cell_counts(records, by = "heart_failure")
nis_suppress(cells, count_col = "n", hospital_col = "hospitals")
#> # A tibble: 2 × 3
#>   heart_failure n     hospitals
#>   <lgl>         <chr> <chr>    
#> 1 FALSE         84    24       
#> 2 TRUE          108   18

Suppressed rows either meet the configured small-cell threshold or represent fewer than two hospitals. Review derived totals and follow the applicable HCUP Data Use Agreement. See Disclosure and suppression.

Common pitfalls

Common pitfalls

  • Filtering to the cohort before building the design drops sampled hospital-years with no cohort records.
  • Treating the invented fixture’s estimates as national results.
  • Sharing a masked table without reviewing totals and other derivable cells.

The exported nis_new_study() helper can copy a Quarto study skeleton; its template workflow is deferred. Start with the articles and function reference for a complete analysis workflow.
